label: digit 3 input during the original phase
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the digit 3 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at any position and any sequence length; precision 1.0 and recall ~0.997 on dev. It does not fire on any other token (other digits and letters essentially never), on the <DEL> step, or when 3 is fed back as input during the copy phase (only ~240 weak copy-phase activations, ~0.15 of max, mostly 3 or 2 right after <DEL>). Activation is fairly uniform (median 0.57, max 0.73); in the examples, the strongest activations are a single 3 late in the sequence, and a 3 that follows an earlier 3 tends to be weaker (about 0.6-0.8 of max).

issues: The core predicate holds on the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.997, F1 0.9985, mass recall 0.9994, correlation 0.995, and 0 false positives. Activation is 0 at the delimiter step. There are 243 copy-phase activations on dev, all weak (about 0.14-0.17 of max). Copy-phase 3s as a whole score precision 0.003, so the 'does not fire on a fed-back 3' claim stands.

The detail about what the misses are is a little off. The 318 test misses hold only 0.1% of the activation mass. They are a 3 fed back at the first copy-phase input (recall_idx 1, when orig(0)=3), plus about 80 weak activations on a 2 in the original phase (several at the last original step just before <DEL>). They are not mostly '3 or 2 just after <DEL>': the 2s come before <DEL>. Either way this is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The magnitude claim that the strongest activations are a single 3 late in the sequence is misleading across the whole dataset. A 3 at t<=1 covers 92% of the top activation quartile and 0% of the bottom two quartiles. A 3 at t>=5 covers only 7% of the top quartile. The single highest examples are late 3s (t=7-8, about 1.0 of max), but the typical strong activations are early 3s.

Earlier tokens weaken the activation, which supports the 'earlier 3 is weaker' observation and goes further. A 3 that follows an earlier 3 covers 16% of the bottom quartile but only 3% of the top. A 3 that follows any earlier digit covers 43% of the bottom quartile but only 8% of the top. So magnitude falls when digits appear earlier in the sequence, not only earlier 3s. None of this changes the binary label.
